Definition: from G1125; a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning:--bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.
BiblicalUsage: grámma means bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written. In Luke 16:6, the text says "Take thy bill." In John 5:47, the text says "But if ye believe not his writings."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading grámma this way, I believe God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Dishonest Manager; Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
